text.q_o182: What do you knock down in bowling? Is it Blocks? Pins? Or Cans?
text.f_o182: Knocking all the pins down on the first try is a strike.
text.q_o183: What do you call it when you run all the way around the bases in baseball on one hit? Is it A touchdown? A home run? Or A goal?
text.a_o183: The answer is A home run.
text.f_o183: There are four bases in baseball.
text.h_o183: The ball usually goes over the fence.
text.q_o184: How many players are on a soccer team on the field? Is it 20? 5? Or 11?
text.f_o184: One of the eleven is the goalkeeper.
text.q_o185: What is the biggest ocean? Is it Pacific Ocean? Atlantic Ocean? Or Indian Ocean?
text.f_o185: The Pacific Ocean is bigger than all the land on Earth put together.
text.h_o185: It's on the west side of America.
text.q_o186: What country do we live in? Is it Canada? The United States? Or Mexico?
text.a_o186: The answer is The United States.
text.f_o186: The United States flag has 50 stars.
text.q_o187: How many stars are on the American flag? Is it 100? 13? Or 50?
text.f_o187: The 13 stripes stand for the first 13 colonies.
text.q_o188: What are the colors of the American flag? Is it Black and orange? Red, white, and blue? Or Green and yellow?
text.a_o188: The answer is Red, white, and blue.
text.f_o188: The flag is nicknamed the Stars and Stripes.
text.h_o188: Think of the Fourth of July.
text.q_o189: What is a really tall hill with a pointy top called? Is it A mountain? A valley? Or A lake?
text.f_o189: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain in the world.
text.q_o190: What is a big area of sand with very little rain called? Is it A lake? A jungle? Or A desert?
text.f_o190: Some deserts are cold, like Antarctica.
text.q_o191: What is the coldest continent, covered in ice? Is it Australia? Africa? Or Antarctica?
text.f_o191: Antarctica is at the bottom of the globe.
text.q_o192: What is a map of the whole Earth shaped like a ball called? Is it A ruler? A globe? Or A cube?
text.f_o192: Blue on a globe shows water.
text.q_o193: Which country is just north of the United States? Is it France? Mexico? Or Canada?
text.f_o193: Canada is the second biggest country in the world.
text.h_o193: It has a maple leaf on its flag.
text.q_o194: Which animal lives in Australia and hops? Is it Penguin? Polar bear? Or Kangaroo?
text.f_o194: There are more kangaroos than people in Australia.
text.q_o195: Where does a polar bear live? Is it The desert? The jungle? Or The Arctic?
text.f_o195: Polar bears have black skin under their white fur.
text.q_o196: What is the name of the big statue holding a torch in New York? Is it The Statue of Liberty? The Big Lady? Or The Torch Tower?
text.a_o196: The answer is The Statue of Liberty.
text.f_o196: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France.
text.q_o197: What letter does apple start with? Is it A? P? Or B?
text.f_o197: A is the first letter of the alphabet.
text.q_o198: What letter does ball start with? Is it B? P? Or D?
text.f_o198: B is the second letter of the alphabet.
text.q_o199: How many letters are in the alphabet? Is it 20? 26? Or 30?
text.f_o199: The letters E and A are some of the most used.
text.q_o200: Which word rhymes with cat? Is it Hat? Cup? Or Dog?
text.f_o200: Rhyming words sound the same at the end.
text.q_o201: Which word rhymes with bee? Is it Tree? Fly? Or Bug?
text.f_o201: Dr. Seuss wrote lots of rhyming books.
text.q_o202: Which word rhymes with cake? Is it Cookie? Lake? Or Pie?
text.f_o202: Rhymes make songs and poems fun.
text.q_o203: What is the opposite of hot? Is it Warm? Wet? Or Cold?
text.f_o203: Opposites are words that mean totally different things.
text.q_o204: What is the opposite of up? Is it High? Over? Or Down?
text.h_o204: Which way does a ball fall?
text.q_o205: What is the opposite of big? Is it Huge? Little? Or Tall?
text.f_o205: Small means the same as little.
text.q_o206: What letter comes after A? Is it B? C? Or Z?
text.f_o206: The alphabet song helps you remember the order.
text.q_o207: What is the last letter of the alphabet? Is it A? Z? Or Y?
text.f_o207: Z is one of the least used letters.
text.q_o208: Which letter is a vowel? Is it B? T? Or E?
text.f_o208: Every word needs at least one vowel sound.
text.h_o208: The vowels are A, E, I, O, U.
text.q_o209: Which word rhymes with moon? Is it Sun? Star? Or Spoon?
text.f_o209: The cow jumped over the moon in a nursery rhyme.
text.q_o210: Which dinosaur had three horns on its face? Is it Triceratops? T. rex? Or Stegosaurus?
text.q_o211: Which dinosaur had plates on its back and spikes on its tail? Is it Stegosaurus? Triceratops? Or Brontosaurus?
text.f_o211: Stegosaurus had a tiny brain for such a big body.
text.h_o211: Its back looked like a row of kites.
text.q_o212: Which dinosaur had tiny arms and a big head? Is it Triceratops? Ankylosaurus? Or T. rex?
text.f_o212: T. rex had teeth as big as bananas.
text.h_o212: Its name means tyrant lizard king.
text.q_o213: Which long-necked dinosaur ate leaves from tall trees? Is it Brontosaurus? Velociraptor? Or T. rex?
text.f_o213: Long-necked dinosaurs were some of the biggest animals ever.
text.q_o214: How do we learn about dinosaurs today? Is it From fossils? From videos? Or From the zoo?
text.f_o214: People who study fossils are called paleontologists.
text.q_o215: Which flying reptile lived with the dinosaurs? Is it Bat? Pterodactyl? Or Parrot?
text.f_o215: Pterodactyls were not dinosaurs, but cousins of them.
text.q_o216: What vehicle travels on tracks and has a caboose? Is it A boat? A train? Or A bus?
text.f_o216: The caboose is the last car of a train.
text.q_o217: What do cars need to fill up so they can go? Is it Gas or electricity? Milk? Or Water?
text.a_o217: The answer is Gas or electricity.
text.f_o217: Electric cars plug in to charge.
text.q_o218: What does a pilot fly? Is it An airplane? A train? Or A truck?
text.f_o218: The Wright brothers flew the first airplane in 1903.
text.q_o219: What kind of boat goes under the water? Is it A canoe? A submarine? Or A raft?
text.f_o219: Submarines can stay underwater for months.
text.q_o220: What do you call a truck that mixes concrete? Is it A tow truck? A cement mixer? Or A taxi?
text.a_o220: The answer is A cement mixer.
text.f_o220: The drum spins so the concrete doesn't get hard.
text.h_o220: Its drum spins around and around.
text.q_s001: What is the largest continent? Is it Asia? North America? Or Africa?
text.f_s001: More people live in Asia than on all the other continents combined.
text.h_s001: China and India are on it.
text.q_s002: What is the longest river in the world? Is it The Mississippi? The Nile? Or The Snake?
text.f_s002: Some scientists say the Amazon might be just a bit longer.
text.q_s003: Which continent is the United States on? Is it Europe? South America? Or North America?
text.f_s003: North America is the third largest continent.
text.h_s003: Canada and Mexico are on it too.
text.q_s004: How many continents are there? Is it 7? 9? Or 5?
text.f_s004: Antarctica is the only continent with no countries.
text.h_s004: Count: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia.
text.q_s005: What is the capital of the United States? Is it New York City? Los Angeles? Or Washington, D.C.?
text.f_s005: D.C. stands for District of Columbia.
text.q_s006: Which state is the largest by area? Is it Texas? California? Or Alaska?
text.f_s006: Alaska is more than twice as big as Texas.
text.h_s006: It's way up north near Canada.
text.q_s007: Which state is made up of islands in the Pacific Ocean? Is it Florida? Maine? Or Hawaii?
text.f_s007: Hawaii was the 50th state to join the U.S.
text.q_s008: What is the smallest state? Is it Connecticut? Rhode Island? Or Delaware?
text.f_s008: You can drive across Rhode Island in about an hour.
text.h_s008: Its name has the word island in it.
text.q_s009: On which continent is Egypt? Is it Asia? Africa? Or Europe?
text.q_s010: What is the capital of France? Is it Rome? London? Or Paris?
text.f_s010: The Eiffel Tower was built for a world's fair in 1889.
text.q_s011: Which country is shaped like a boot? Is it Spain? Italy? Or Greece?
text.f_s011: Rome, the capital of Italy, is nearly 3,000 years old.
text.h_s011: Pizza and pasta come from there.
text.q_s012: In which country would you find the Great Wall? Is it China? Japan? Or India?
text.f_s012: The Great Wall is thousands of miles long.
text.q_s013: Which ocean is between the United States and Europe? Is it Pacific Ocean? Atlantic Ocean? Or Arctic Ocean?
text.f_s013: The Atlantic is the second largest ocean.
text.h_s013: You cross it to fly from New York to London.
text.q_s014: What is the tallest mountain in the world? Is it Mount Everest? Mount Rainier? Or Mount Fuji?
text.f_s014: Mount Everest is about 29,000 feet tall.
text.q_s015: Which country is south of the United States? Is it Canada? Mexico? Or Brazil?
text.f_s015: Mexico City is built on top of an old lake.
text.q_s016: What is the biggest desert that's hot? Is it The Sahara? The Gobi? Or The Mojave?
text.f_s016: The Sahara is about as big as the whole United States.
text.q_s017: Which river flows past St. Louis and New Orleans? Is it The Colorado? The Mississippi? Or The Hudson?
text.f_s017: The Mississippi River starts as a tiny stream in Minnesota.
text.h_s017: It has four S's in its name.
text.q_s018: What is the capital of Japan? Is it Tokyo? Beijing? Or Seoul?
text.f_s018: Japan is made of thousands of islands.
text.h_s018: It's one of the biggest cities in the world.
text.q_s019: Which country has kangaroos and koalas? Is it Australia? India? Or Brazil?
text.f_s019: Australia is the only country that is also a whole continent.
text.q_s020: What line divides the Earth into northern and southern halves? Is it The North Pole? The equator? Or The time zone?
text.f_s020: The equator is about 25,000 miles around.
text.q_s021: What is the name for a piece of land surrounded by water? Is it An island? A canyon? Or A peninsula?
text.f_s021: Greenland is the largest island in the world.
text.q_s022: What famous canyon did the Colorado River carve? Is it Copper Canyon? The Grand Canyon? Or Bryce Canyon?
text.a_s022: The answer is The Grand Canyon.
text.f_s022: The Grand Canyon is about a mile deep.
text.q_s023: Which direction does the sun rise? Is it West? North? Or East?
text.f_s023: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
text.h_s023: The sun sets in the opposite direction.
text.q_s024: What are the five Great Lakes near? Is it Florida? Canada? Or Mexico?
text.f_s024: Lake Superior is the biggest of the Great Lakes.
text.q_s025: What is the capital of England? Is it Dublin? London? Or Paris?
text.f_s025: Big Ben is actually the name of the bell, not the tower.
text.q_s026: Which South American rainforest is the largest in the world? Is it The Sahara? The Amazon? Or The Congo?
text.f_s026: The Amazon rainforest is home to millions of kinds of bugs.
text.h_s026: It shares its name with a river.
text.q_s027: What is a narrow strip of land with water on three sides? Is it An island? A peninsula? Or A plateau?
text.f_s027: Florida's peninsula sticks out between the Atlantic and the Gulf.
text.q_s028: Which state is known as the Sunshine State? Is it Arizona? Florida? Or California?
text.f_s028: Florida has more coastline than any state except Alaska.
text.h_s028: It has orange groves and Disney World.
text.q_s029: Where is Mount Rushmore? Is it South Dakota? Idaho? Or Colorado?
text.f_s029: Mount Rushmore shows four presidents carved in stone.
text.q_s030: Which planet is called the Red Planet? Is it Mercury? Neptune? Or Mars?
text.f_s030: Mars has the biggest volcano in the solar system.
text.q_s031: Which planet is the hottest? Is it Venus? Mercury? Or Mars?
text.f_s031: Thick clouds trap heat on Venus, making it hotter than Mercury.
text.h_s031: It's the second planet from the Sun.
text.q_s032: Which planet spins on its side? Is it Jupiter? Saturn? Or Uranus?
text.f_s032: Uranus may have been knocked over by a huge crash long ago.
text.q_s033: Which planet is farthest from the Sun? Is it Neptune? Pluto? Or Uranus?
text.f_s033: Neptune has the fastest winds in the solar system.
text.q_s034: What is the Great Red Spot on Jupiter? Is it A giant storm? A volcano? Or A lake?
text.a_s034: The answer is A giant storm.
text.f_s034: The Great Red Spot is bigger than Earth.
text.h_s034: It's been swirling for hundreds of years.
text.q_s035: What is a group of stars that makes a picture called? Is it A constellation? A galaxy? Or A comet?
text.f_s035: Orion is a constellation shaped like a hunter.
text.h_s035: The Big Dipper is part of one.
text.q_s036: What do we call a ball of ice and dust with a long glowing tail? Is it A moon? A comet? Or An asteroid?
text.f_s036: Halley's Comet comes back about every 76 years.
text.q_s037: What is the name of the space station where astronauts live? Is it The International Space Station? The Star Hotel? Or The Moon Base?
text.a_s037: The answer is The International Space Station.
text.f_s037: The ISS circles the Earth about 16 times a day.
text.q_s038: How long does it take the Earth to go around the Sun? Is it One year? One month? Or One day?
text.f_s038: Every four years we add a leap day, February 29th.
text.q_s039: How long does it take the Earth to spin once? Is it One year? One day? Or One week?
text.f_s039: The spin of the Earth gives us day and night.
text.q_s040: What was the name of the program that landed people on the Moon? Is it Gemini? Mercury? Or Apollo?
text.f_s040: Twelve astronauts have walked on the Moon.
text.q_s041: Who was the first American woman in space? Is it Rosa Parks? Sally Ride? Or Amelia Earhart?
text.f_s041: Sally Ride later wrote science books for kids.
text.h_s041: She flew on the space shuttle in 1983.
text.q_s042: What is the Sun mostly made of? Is it Hydrogen and helium gas? Fire and wood? Or Rock?
text.a_s042: The answer is Hydrogen and helium gas.
text.f_s042: The Sun's light takes about eight minutes to reach us.
text.h_s042: It's a giant ball of gas.
text.q_s043: Which planet has the most moons that we know of? Is it Earth? Saturn? Or Mars?
text.f_s043: Saturn has well over 200 known moons.
text.q_s044: What is the name of Mars rover that landed in 2021? Is it Perseverance? Voyager? Or Curiosity?
text.f_s044: Perseverance carried a little helicopter named Ingenuity.
text.h_s044: Its name means to keep trying.
text.q_s045: What do we call a space rock that lands on Earth? Is it A satellite? A meteorite? Or A comet?
text.f_s045: Most meteorites come from the asteroid belt.
text.h_s045: It used to be a shooting star.
text.q_s046: Between which two planets is the asteroid belt? Is it Earth and Mars? Saturn and Uranus? Or Mars and Jupiter?
text.a_s046: The answer is Mars and Jupiter.
text.f_s046: The biggest object in the asteroid belt is Ceres.
text.h_s046: It's between the rocky planets and the gas giants.
text.q_s047: Which phase is it when the whole Moon looks bright? Is it Half moon? Full moon? Or New moon?
text.f_s047: The Moon doesn't make its own light. It reflects sunlight.
text.q_s048: Who was the first President of the United States? Is it Thomas Jefferson? George Washington? Or Abraham Lincoln?
text.f_s048: George Washington never lived in the White House.
text.h_s048: His face is on the one-dollar bill.
text.q_s049: Which President is on the five-dollar bill? Is it George Washington? Abraham Lincoln? Or John Adams?
text.h_s049: He wore a tall top hat.
text.q_s050: In what year was the Declaration of Independence signed? Is it 1776? 1812? Or 1492?
text.f_s050: Thomas Jefferson wrote most of the Declaration.
text.h_s050: The U.S. turned 250 years old in 2026.
text.q_s051: Who sailed to the Americas in 1492? Is it Christopher Columbus? Paul Revere? Or Neil Armstrong?
text.f_s051: Columbus was trying to reach Asia.
text.h_s051: His ships were the Niña, Pinta, and Santa María.
text.q_s052: Who invented the light bulb that lasted a long time? Is it Benjamin Franklin? Henry Ford? Or Thomas Edison?
text.h_s052: His lab was in Menlo Park.
text.q_s053: Who flew a kite in a storm to study electricity? Is it George Washington? Thomas Edison? Or Benjamin Franklin?
text.q_s054: Which explorers traveled across Idaho with Sacagawea? Is it Wright brothers? Lewis and Clark? Or Columbus and Magellan?
text.a_s054: The answer is Lewis and Clark.
text.f_s054: Sacagawea was a Shoshone woman who helped guide them.
text.q_s055: Who were the first to fly an airplane? Is it The Jonas Brothers? The Wright brothers? Or Lewis and Clark?
text.a_s055: The answer is The Wright brothers.
text.f_s055: Their first flight lasted only 12 seconds.
text.h_s055: Their names were Orville and Wilbur.
text.q_s056: What did the Pilgrims sail on in 1620? Is it The Titanic? The Santa María? Or The Mayflower?
text.h_s056: Its name has a flower in it.
text.q_s057: Which ancient people built the pyramids at Giza? Is it The Vikings? The Egyptians? Or The Romans?
text.f_s057: The Great Pyramid was the tallest building on Earth for thousands of years.
text.q_s058: Who gave the I Have a Dream speech? Is it Benjamin Franklin? Abraham Lincoln? Or Martin Luther King Jr.?
text.a_s058: The answer is Martin Luther King Jr..
text.f_s058: He gave the speech in Washington, D.C., in 1963.
text.h_s058: We have a holiday for him in January.
text.q_s059: What did Rosa Parks refuse to give up on a bus? Is it Her seat? Her umbrella? Or Her ticket?
text.f_s059: Rosa Parks is called the mother of the civil rights movement.
text.q_s060: Where does the President live? Is it The White House? The Pentagon? Or The Capitol?
text.a_s060: The answer is The White House.
text.q_s061: What did ancient Romans build to carry water to their cities? Is it Canals? Pipelines? Or Aqueducts?
text.f_s061: Some Roman aqueducts are still standing today.
text.h_s061: The word starts with aqua, meaning water.
text.q_s062: Who rode at night to warn that the British were coming? Is it Ben Franklin? George Washington? Or Paul Revere?
text.h_s062: He was a silversmith in Boston.
text.q_s063: Which Viking explorer may have reached North America around the year 1000? Is it Christopher Columbus? Leif Erikson? Or Marco Polo?
text.h_s063: His dad was Erik the Red.
text.q_s064: Which document begins with We the People? Is it The Bill of Rights? The Constitution? Or The Declaration of Independence?
text.h_s064: It's the plan for the U.S. government.
text.q_s065: How many original colonies were there? Is it 50? 10? Or 13?
text.f_s065: Delaware was the first state to join.
text.h_s065: There's one stripe for each on the flag.
text.q_s066: What is the plural of mouse? Is it Mouses? Meese? Or Mice?
text.f_s066: The plural of a computer mouse can be mice or mouses.
text.q_s067: What is the plural of child? Is it Children? Childs? Or Childrens?
text.f_s067: Long ago, the plural of child was childer.
text.h_s067: Kids are another word for them.
text.q_s068: Which letter is silent in the word knight? Is it K? T? Or N?
text.f_s068: Long ago, people did say the K in knight.
text.q_s069: Which letter is silent in the word lamb? Is it L? B? Or M?
text.f_s069: Comb, thumb, and climb also have a silent B.
text.q_s070: What is the plural of goose? Is it Geese? Geeses? Or Gooses?
text.f_s070: A group of geese on the ground is called a gaggle.
text.q_s071: What is the plural of tooth? Is it Teeths? Tooths? Or Teeth?
text.q_s072: Which word means the same as happy? Is it Joyful? Sleepy? Or Grumpy?
text.f_s072: Words that mean the same thing are called synonyms.
text.q_s073: Which word means the opposite of ancient? Is it Old? Modern? Or Antique?
text.f_s073: Words with opposite meanings are called antonyms.
text.q_s074: Flower and flour sound the same. What do we call words like that? Is it Antonyms? Synonyms? Or Homophones?
text.f_s074: Pair and pear are homophones too.
text.h_s074: Homo means same and phone means sound.
text.q_s075: Which word is a noun? Is it Run? Elephant? Or Quickly?
text.f_s075: Proper nouns, like Boise, start with a capital letter.
text.h_s075: A noun is a person, place, or thing.
text.q_s076: Which word is a verb? Is it Happy? Jump? Or Table?
text.f_s076: Is, am, and are are verbs too.
text.q_s077: Which word is an adjective? Is it Purple? Swim? Or Slowly?
text.f_s077: Adjectives usually come before a noun.
text.q_s078: Which word is a compound word? Is it Sunflower? Happy? Or Running?
text.f_s078: Butterfly, rainbow, and football are compound words too.
text.q_s079: Which letter is silent in the word write? Is it T? R? Or W?
text.f_s079: Wrist, wrap, and wrong also start with a silent W.
text.q_s080: What do you call the part of a word added to the beginning, like un in undo? Is it A vowel? A suffix? Or A prefix?
text.f_s080: Re means again, like in redo.
text.q_s081: How many syllables are in the word butterfly? Is it 4? 2? Or 3?
text.f_s081: A syllable is a beat in a word.
text.q_s082: What is the past tense of run? Is it Ran? Runned? Or Running?
text.f_s082: Words like run that change in the past tense are called irregular verbs.
text.q_s083: Which punctuation mark goes at the end of a question? Is it A comma? A period? Or A question mark?
text.a_s083: The answer is A question mark.
text.f_s083: Spanish puts an upside-down question mark at the start, too.
text.h_s083: It looks like a hook with a dot.
text.q_s084: What is the plural of leaf? Is it Leaves? Leafes? Or Leafs?
text.f_s084: Wolf becomes wolves, and calf becomes calves.
text.h_s084: The F turns into a V.
text.q_s085: Which word means very, very big? Is it Tiny? Enormous? Or Narrow?
text.f_s085: Gigantic, huge, and massive mean the same thing.
text.q_s086: What is a word that sounds like what it means, like buzz or splash? Is it Rhyme? Alliteration? Or Onomatopoeia?
text.f_s086: Boom, sizzle, and hiss are onomatopoeia too.
text.q_s087: What gas do we breathe in to stay alive? Is it Oxygen? Carbon dioxide? Or Helium?
text.f_s087: About one fifth of the air is oxygen.
text.q_s088: What gas do plants take in from the air? Is it Carbon dioxide? Oxygen? Or Helium?
text.f_s088: Plants use carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight to make food.
text.h_s088: It's the gas we breathe out.
text.q_s089: What is it called when plants make food from sunlight? Is it Hibernation? Migration? Or Photosynthesis?
text.f_s089: Chlorophyll makes plants green and helps them catch sunlight.
text.q_s090: At what temperature does water boil in Fahrenheit? Is it 100 degrees? 212 degrees? Or 32 degrees?
text.q_s091: What is the hardest natural material on Earth? Is it Gold? Diamond? Or Iron?
text.f_s091: Diamonds are made of carbon squeezed deep underground.
text.q_s092: What force pulls things toward the Earth? Is it Friction? Gravity? Or Magnetism?
text.f_s092: You would weigh much less on the Moon because its gravity is weaker.
text.q_s093: What do we call animals that eat only plants? Is it Omnivores? Carnivores? Or Herbivores?
text.q_s094: What do we call animals that eat both plants and meat? Is it Herbivores? Omnivores? Or Carnivores?
text.q_s095: What is it called when animals sleep through the winter? Is it Migration? Hibernation? Or Camouflage?
text.f_s095: Some hibernating animals' hearts beat only a few times a minute.
text.q_s096: What is it called when birds fly south for the winter? Is it Adaptation? Migration? Or Hibernation?
text.f_s096: Arctic terns migrate farther than any other bird.
text.q_s097: What is the center of an atom called? Is it The nucleus? The cell? Or The shell?
text.f_s097: Atoms are so tiny that millions fit across the width of a hair.
text.q_s098: What are the three states of matter? Is it Rock, paper, and scissors? Hot, warm, and cold? Or Solid, liquid, and gas?
text.a_s098: The answer is Solid, liquid, and gas.
text.f_s098: Plasma, like in lightning, is a fourth state.
text.h_s098: Ice, water, and steam are examples.
text.q_s099: Which tool makes small things look bigger? Is it A telescope? A microscope? Or A thermometer?
text.f_s099: Some microscopes can make things look a million times bigger.
text.h_s099: Scientists use it to see cells.
text.q_s100: What do we call the layer of gases around the Earth? Is it The atmosphere? The core? Or The crust?
text.f_s100: The atmosphere protects us from the Sun's harmful rays.
text.q_s101: What is the hot liquid rock inside a volcano called? Is it Magma? Lava? Or Granite?
text.f_s101: Idaho's Craters of the Moon was made by ancient lava flows.
text.h_s101: When it comes out, we call it lava.
text.q_s102: Which simple machine is a ramp? Is it An inclined plane? A lever? Or A pulley?
text.a_s102: The answer is An inclined plane.
text.f_s102: A slide at the park is an inclined plane.
text.h_s102: It helps you roll things up.
text.q_s103: What kind of energy comes from the Sun and powers solar panels? Is it Nuclear energy? Solar energy? Or Wind energy?
text.f_s103: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity.
text.q_s104: What causes the seasons on Earth? Is it The tilt of the Earth? The distance to the Moon? Or The wind?
text.a_s104: The answer is The tilt of the Earth.
text.f_s104: When your half of Earth tilts toward the Sun, it's summer.
text.h_s104: The Earth leans a little to the side.
text.q_s105: What is a scientist who studies rocks called? Is it A geologist? An astronomer? Or A biologist?
text.q_s106: Which part of a plant makes seeds? Is it The stem? The root? Or The flower?
text.f_s106: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower.
text.q_s107: What do we call it when water vapor turns into liquid drops? Is it Melting? Evaporation? Or Condensation?
text.h_s107: It's the drops on a cold glass.
text.q_s108: Which travels faster, light or sound? Is it They're the same? Light? Or Sound?
text.f_s108: Light can go around the Earth more than seven times in one second.
text.h_s108: That's why you see lightning before thunder.
text.q_s109: What is 6 times 7? Is it 42? 36? Or 48?
text.q_s110: What is 8 times 8? Is it 72? 64? Or 56?
text.q_s111: What is 9 times 3? Is it 24? 30? Or 27?
text.f_s111: The digits of 27 add up to 9, like all multiples of 9.
text.q_s112: What is 12 times 2? Is it 24? 22? Or 26?
text.f_s112: There are 24 hours in a day.
text.q_s113: What is 5 times 9? Is it 40? 45? Or 50?
text.f_s113: Numbers times 5 always end in 0 or 5.
text.q_s114: What is 7 times 7? Is it 49? 42? Or 56?
text.f_s114: 7 times 7 is the same as 7 squared.
text.q_s115: What is 4 times 6? Is it 28? 24? Or 20?
text.q_s116: What is 3 times 8? Is it 21? 27? Or 24?
text.f_s116: A spider's legs times three equals 24.
text.q_s117: What is 10 times 10? Is it 10? 1,000? Or 100?
text.f_s117: A hundred years is called a century.
text.q_s118: What is 11 times 11? Is it 111? 121? Or 122?
text.f_s118: 11 times 11 is a palindrome, the same forward and backward.
text.q_s119: What is 9 times 9? Is it 81? 99? Or 72?
text.f_s119: 81 is the biggest answer you can get multiplying two one-digit numbers.
text.q_s120: What is 6 times 8? Is it 48? 54? Or 42?
text.q_s121: What is 36 divided by 6? Is it 6? 5? Or 7?
text.f_s121: Division is the opposite of multiplication.
text.q_s122: What is 56 divided by 8? Is it 8? 7? Or 6?
text.q_s123: What is 100 divided by 4? Is it 40? 20? Or 25?
text.h_s123: There are four quarters in a dollar.
text.q_s124: What is half of 50? Is it 25? 30? Or 20?
text.h_s124: Split it into two equal parts.
text.q_s125: How many sides does a pentagon have? Is it 6? 8? Or 5?
text.f_s125: The Pentagon building has five sides.
text.q_s126: How many minutes are in two hours? Is it 200? 60? Or 120?
text.f_s126: There are 1,440 minutes in a day.
text.h_s126: There are 60 minutes in one hour.
text.q_s127: How many inches are in one foot? Is it 100? 10? Or 12?
text.q_s128: How many feet are in a yard? Is it 3? 12? Or 10?
text.f_s128: A football field is 100 yards long between the goal lines.
text.h_s128: A yard is a bit shorter than a meter.
text.q_s129: What is a fraction for one out of two equal parts? Is it One third? One fourth? Or One half?
text.h_s129: It's what you get when you split something in two.
text.q_s130: Which fraction is bigger, one half or one fourth? Is it One fourth? One half? Or They're the same?
text.f_s130: A bigger bottom number means smaller pieces.
text.q_s131: What is the value of 3 quarters? Is it 50 cents? 75 cents? Or 30 cents?
text.q_s132: What do you call an angle that is exactly 90 degrees? Is it A right angle? An obtuse angle? Or An acute angle?
text.a_s132: The answer is A right angle.
text.f_s132: Acute angles are smaller than 90 degrees.
text.q_s133: Which number is a prime number? Is it 9? 8? Or 7?
text.f_s133: 2 is the only even prime number.
text.h_s133: It can only be divided by 1 and itself.
text.q_s134: What is 1,000 minus 1? Is it 990? 900? Or 999?
text.f_s134: 999 is the biggest number with three digits.
text.q_s135: How many sides does an octagon have? Is it 8? 10? Or 6?
text.f_s135: Octo means eight, like an octopus.
text.q_s136: What is the perimeter of a square with sides of 5 inches? Is it 20 inches? 25 inches? Or 10 inches?
text.f_s136: Area is different. It's 5 times 5, or 25 square inches.
text.q_s137: How many days are in a leap year? Is it 364? 365? Or 366?
text.q_s138: What is 15 plus 15? Is it 30? 35? Or 25?
text.f_s138: There are about 30 days in a month.
text.q_s139: What is the fastest land animal? Is it Horse? Lion? Or Cheetah?
text.f_s139: A cheetah can sprint around 60 to 70 miles per hour.
text.q_s140: What is the largest animal that ever lived? Is it T. rex? Blue whale? Or African elephant?
text.f_s140: A blue whale's tongue can weigh as much as an elephant.
text.h_s140: It lives in the ocean today.
text.q_s141: How many hearts does an octopus have? Is it 1? 3? Or 8?
text.q_s142: What kind of animal is a whale? Is it A fish? A reptile? Or A mammal?
text.f_s142: Whales breathe through blowholes on top of their heads.
text.h_s142: It breathes air and feeds its babies milk.
text.q_s143: What is a group of lions called? Is it A pride? A herd? Or A pack?
text.f_s143: Lionesses do most of the hunting.
text.h_s143: It's also a word for feeling proud.
text.q_s144: What is a group of whales called? Is it A pod? A school? Or A gaggle?
text.f_s144: Orcas live in family pods for their whole lives.
text.h_s144: It's also what peas come in.
text.q_s145: Which animal is the tallest in the world? Is it Elephant? Giraffe? Or Ostrich?
text.f_s145: Giraffes only need about two hours of sleep a day.
text.h_s145: It has a really long neck.
text.q_s146: Which bird is the largest in the world? Is it Eagle? Ostrich? Or Penguin?
text.f_s146: An ostrich egg is as big as about two dozen chicken eggs.
text.h_s146: It can't fly but runs fast.
text.q_s147: What do you call an animal that is active at night? Is it Nocturnal? Hibernating? Or Diurnal?
text.f_s147: Diurnal animals are awake during the day.
text.q_s148: What is a baby goat called? Is it A foal? A kid? Or A calf?
text.h_s148: It's also a word for a child.
text.q_s149: Which mammal can fly? Is it Flying squirrel? Penguin? Or Bat?
text.f_s149: Flying squirrels only glide. They can't really fly.
text.q_s150: How do snakes smell? Is it With their tongues? With their ears? Or With their tails?
text.a_s150: The answer is With their tongues.
text.h_s150: They flick it in and out.
text.q_s151: What is a frog that lives mostly on land and has bumpy skin called? Is it A toad? A lizard? Or A newt?
text.f_s151: All toads are frogs, but not all frogs are toads.
text.q_s152: Which animal is known for building dams in rivers? Is it Otter? Bear? Or Beaver?
text.f_s152: Beavers' teeth are orange because they contain iron.
text.h_s152: It has big front teeth and a flat tail.
text.q_s153: What are animals with backbones called? Is it Insects? Vertebrates? Or Invertebrates?
text.f_s153: Most animals on Earth are invertebrates, like insects.
text.q_s154: What do caterpillars turn into inside a chrysalis? Is it Beetles? Bees? Or Butterflies?
text.f_s154: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles to Mexico.
text.q_s155: Which sea creature has no brain, no heart, and no bones? Is it Shark? Dolphin? Or Jellyfish?
text.f_s155: Jellyfish have been around longer than dinosaurs.
text.h_s155: It can sting and floats in the ocean.
text.q_s156: How many bones are in an adult's body? Is it 306? 206? Or 106?
text.f_s156: Babies are born with about 300 bones, and some fuse together.
text.q_s157: Which organs fill with air when you breathe? Is it Lungs? Kidneys? Or Stomach?
text.f_s157: Your left lung is a bit smaller to make room for your heart.
text.h_s157: They're in your chest behind your ribs.
text.q_s158: What is the largest organ of your body? Is it Brain? Heart? Or Skin?
text.f_s158: You shed tiny skin flakes every day.
text.h_s158: It covers you from head to toe.
text.q_s159: What is the longest bone in your body? Is it Thigh bone? Arm bone? Or Backbone?
text.f_s159: The thigh bone is called the femur.
text.q_s160: Where is the smallest bone in your body? Is it In your toe? In your nose? Or In your ear?
text.a_s160: The answer is In your ear.
text.f_s160: The smallest bone, the stirrup, is about the size of a grain of rice.
text.q_s161: Which blood cells fight germs? Is it White blood cells? Red blood cells? Or Platelets?
text.a_s161: The answer is White blood cells.
text.q_s162: What part of your eye is colored? Is it The lens? The iris? Or The pupil?
text.f_s162: The pupil is the black dot that gets bigger in the dark.
text.h_s162: It can be blue, brown, or green.
text.q_s163: How many teeth does an adult usually have? Is it 42? 20? Or 32?
text.f_s163: Wisdom teeth are the last ones to grow in.
text.q_s164: What does your brain use to send messages around your body? Is it Nerves? Bones? Or Muscles?
text.f_s164: Nerve messages can travel over 200 miles per hour.
text.q_s165: What vitamin does your body make from sunlight? Is it Vitamin C? Vitamin A? Or Vitamin D?
text.f_s165: Vitamin C is found in oranges.
text.q_s166: Which organ cleans your blood and makes pee? Is it Kidneys? Heart? Or Lungs?
text.f_s166: Kidneys are about the size of your fist.
text.h_s166: You have two of them, shaped like beans.
text.q_s167: What is the strongest muscle for its size? Is it Jaw muscle? Arm muscle? Or Leg muscle?
text.f_s167: The jaw muscle is called the masseter.
text.q_s168: In Moana, what is the name of the demigod? Is it Te Fiti? Tamatoa? Or Maui?
text.f_s168: Maui is voiced by Dwayne The Rock Johnson.
text.q_s169: In Frozen, what is the name of Elsa's ice palace song? Is it Do You Want to Build a Snowman? Let It Go? Or Into the Unknown?
text.a_s169: The answer is Let It Go.
text.f_s169: Let It Go won an Oscar for Best Original Song.
text.h_s169: She sings it on the North Mountain.
text.q_s170: In Zootopia, what kind of animal is Judy Hopps? Is it A rabbit? A sheep? Or A fox?
text.q_s171: What is the name of the robot in a movie about a lonely trash-collecting robot? Is it Baymax? R2-D2? Or WALL-E?
text.f_s171: WALL-E has a pet cockroach named Hal.
text.h_s171: His friend is a robot named EVE.
text.q_s172: In Inside Out, which emotion is blue? Is it Anger? Sadness? Or Joy?
text.f_s172: Inside Out 2 added new emotions like Anxiety.
text.q_s173: In Big Hero 6, what is the name of the big white robot? Is it Wall-E? Optimus? Or Baymax?
text.f_s173: Baymax says I am your personal healthcare companion.
text.q_s174: In Coco, what instrument does Miguel want to play? Is it Trumpet? Drums? Or Guitar?
text.f_s174: Coco is about the Day of the Dead in Mexico.
text.q_s175: What is the name of the princess in Tangled? Is it Aurora? Belle? Or Rapunzel?
text.q_s176: In Beauty and the Beast, what is the name of the candlestick? Is it Lumière? Cogsworth? Or Chip?
text.q_s177: Which movie features a house lifted by balloons? Is it Cars? Up? Or Brave?
text.f_s177: The boy scout in Up is named Russell.
text.h_s177: An old man and a Scout fly away.
text.q_s178: In Harry Potter, what sport is played on broomsticks? Is it Polo? Soccer? Or Quidditch?
text.f_s178: Harry plays Seeker for his house team.
text.h_s178: The golden ball is the Snitch.
text.q_s179: What is the name of the snow queen's sister in Frozen? Is it Anna? Elsa? Or Merida?
text.f_s179: Anna and Elsa live in the kingdom of Arendelle.
text.q_s180: In The Little Mermaid, what is Ariel's crab friend's name? Is it Scuttle? Flounder? Or Sebastian?
text.f_s180: Flounder is actually a tropical fish, not a flounder.
text.q_s181: In Kung Fu Panda, what is the panda's name? Is it Tai Lung? Shifu? Or Po?
text.f_s181: Po's dad is a goose who runs a noodle shop.
text.q_s182: In Encanto, what gift does Luisa have? Is it Shape shifting? Healing? Or Super strength?
text.h_s182: She can lift a whole church.
text.q_s183: Which Idaho waterfall is taller than Niagara Falls? Is it Shoshone Falls? Twin Falls? Or Mesa Falls?
text.f_s183: Shoshone Falls on the Snake River is about 212 feet tall.
text.h_s183: People call it the Niagara of the West.
text.q_s184: What is Idaho's nickname? Is it The Lone Star State? The Gem State? Or The Sunshine State?
text.a_s184: The answer is The Gem State.
text.f_s184: Idaho has more than 70 kinds of gemstones.
text.h_s184: Idaho has lots of precious stones.
text.q_s185: Which big river crosses southern Idaho? Is it The Mississippi? The Colorado? Or The Snake River?
text.a_s185: The answer is The Snake River.
text.f_s185: The Snake River is more than 1,000 miles long.
text.h_s185: It's named after a slithery animal.
text.q_s186: What is Idaho's state tree? Is it Palm tree? Western white pine? Or Maple?
text.a_s186: The answer is Western white pine.
text.f_s186: Idaho has the largest stand of western white pine in the U.S.
text.q_s187: What Idaho monument looks like the surface of the Moon? Is it Bear Lake? City of Rocks? Or Craters of the Moon?
text.a_s187: The answer is Craters of the Moon.
text.f_s187: Apollo astronauts trained at Craters of the Moon in 1969.
text.q_s188: Which Idaho city is famous for its ski resort, Sun Valley? Is it Pocatello? Ketchum? Or Boise?
text.f_s188: Sun Valley built some of the world's first chairlifts in 1936.
text.q_s189: Which Idaho park has the tallest single sand dune in North America? Is it Bruneau Dunes? Craters of the Moon? Or Shoshone Falls?
text.f_s189: The tallest dune at Bruneau is about 470 feet tall.
text.q_s190: In what year did Idaho become a state? Is it 1890? 1950? Or 1776?
text.f_s190: Idaho became a state on July 3rd, 1890.
text.q_s191: Which bird of prey has a big center for protecting it near Boise? Is it Peregrine falcon? Parrot? Or Penguin?
text.f_s191: The World Center for Birds of Prey is just south of Boise.
text.h_s191: It's the fastest bird when it dives.
text.q_s192: What is the name of the long biking and walking path along the Boise River? Is it The Greenbelt? The Blueway? Or The Silver Trail?
text.f_s192: The Boise River Greenbelt is over 25 miles long.
text.h_s192: Its name has a color in it.
text.q_s193: How many players are on a basketball team on the court? Is it 5? 6? Or 11?
text.f_s193: Basketball was invented by James Naismith in 1891.
text.q_s194: In which sport would you hear the word love for zero? Is it Tennis? Baseball? Or Golf?
text.f_s194: Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament.
text.q_s195: How many holes are on a regular golf course? Is it 12? 9? Or 18?
text.f_s195: The fewest strokes for a hole is called a hole-in-one.
text.q_s196: Which country hosts the Summer Olympics in 2028? Is it The United States? France? Or Japan?
text.a_s196: The answer is The United States.
text.f_s196: The Olympic rings stand for five parts of the world.
text.h_s196: It will be in Los Angeles.
text.q_s197: How many rings are on the Olympic flag? Is it 6? 4? Or 5?
text.f_s197: The rings are blue, yellow, black, green, and red.
text.h_s197: One for each group of continents.
text.q_s198: What is the championship game of the NFL called? Is it The Stanley Cup? The Super Bowl? Or The World Series?
text.a_s198: The answer is The Super Bowl.
text.f_s198: The Super Bowl winners get the Lombardi Trophy.
text.q_s199: What is the trophy for the NHL hockey champions? Is it The Stanley Cup? The Lombardi Trophy? Or The Gold Cup?
text.a_s199: The answer is The Stanley Cup.
text.f_s199: The Stanley Cup is over 130 years old.
text.h_s199: Every player gets a day with it.
text.q_s200: How many bases are on a baseball field? Is it 4? 5? Or 3?
text.q_s201: What is it called when a bowler knocks down all ten pins on the first ball? Is it A spare? A strike? Or A gutter?
text.f_s201: A perfect bowling game is 300 points.
text.q_s202: In soccer, what is it called when one player scores three goals in a game? Is it A triple play? A hat trick? Or A slam dunk?
text.a_s202: The answer is A hat trick.
text.f_s202: The term hat trick started in cricket.
text.q_s203: How many strings does a regular guitar have? Is it 12? 4? Or 6?
text.f_s203: A bass guitar usually has four strings.
text.q_s204: Which instrument has 88 keys? Is it Piano? Violin? Or Guitar?
text.f_s204: The piano's full name is pianoforte.
text.h_s204: It has black and white keys.
text.q_s205: What do you call a group of musicians playing classical music together? Is it A choir? A band camp? Or An orchestra?
text.f_s205: The conductor leads the orchestra with a baton.
text.h_s205: It has violins, cellos, and more.
text.q_s206: Which instrument do you blow into and has a slide? Is it Drum? Flute? Or Trombone?
text.f_s206: The trombone's slide changes the notes.
text.q_s207: Which famous composer kept writing music after he became deaf? Is it Bach? Beethoven? Or Mozart?
text.f_s207: Beethoven felt vibrations to help him make music.
text.q_s208: How many people sing in a duet? Is it 3? 2? Or 4?
text.q_s209: What is guacamole mostly made from? Is it Pear? Lime? Or Avocado?
text.f_s209: An avocado is actually a big berry.
text.h_s209: It's green inside with a big pit.
text.q_s210: Which country did pizza first come from? Is it Italy? Mexico? Or France?
text.f_s210: The Margherita pizza has the colors of the Italian flag.
text.q_s211: What is the main ingredient in hummus? Is it Peanuts? Chickpeas? Or Potatoes?
text.f_s211: Hummus is from the Middle East.
text.q_s212: Which nut is used to make peanut butter? Is it Peanuts? Almonds? Or Walnuts?
text.f_s212: Peanuts are really legumes, like beans.
text.q_s213: What is the most popular flavor of ice cream in the U.S.? Is it Strawberry? Chocolate? Or Vanilla?
text.f_s213: Vanilla comes from the seed pods of an orchid flower.
text.h_s213: It comes from an orchid bean.
text.q_s214: Which vegetable makes your eyes water when you cut it? Is it Onion? Celery? Or Carrot?
text.f_s214: Onions release a gas that stings your eyes.
text.q_s215: What is tofu made from? Is it Milk? Rice? Or Soybeans?
text.f_s215: Tofu was first made in China long ago.
text.q_s216: What fruit is famous for keeping the doctor away? Is it A banana? An apple? Or A grape?
text.f_s216: There are about 7,500 kinds of apples.
text.q_s217: In what month is Thanksgiving in the United States? Is it November? December? Or October?
text.f_s217: Thanksgiving became a national holiday in 1863 under Lincoln.
text.q_s218: What does the word Halloween come from? Is it All Hallows' Eve? Happy Owl Evening? Or Hollow Weekend?
text.a_s218: The answer is All Hallows' Eve.
text.f_s218: The first jack-o'-lanterns were carved from turnips.
text.h_s218: It's the night before All Saints' Day.
text.q_s219: Which holiday honors the people who serve in the military? Is it Veterans Day? Presidents' Day? Or Labor Day?
text.f_s219: Veterans Day was first called Armistice Day.
text.q_s220: What is the Chinese New Year also called? Is it The Lunar New Year? Winter Day? Or The Sun Festival?
text.a_s220: The answer is The Lunar New Year.
text.f_s220: Each Lunar New Year is named after one of twelve animals.
text.q_s221: How many candles are on a Kwanzaa kinara? Is it 9? 8? Or 7?
text.q_s222: Which holiday is celebrated on the third Monday in January? Is it Martin Luther King Jr. Day? Presidents' Day? Or Memorial Day?
text.a_s222: The answer is Martin Luther King Jr. Day.
text.f_s222: MLK Day became a federal holiday in 1986.
text.h_s222: It honors a civil rights hero.
text.q_s223: What is Idaho's state flower? Is it Sunflower? Syringa? Or Rose?
text.f_s223: Syringa is also called mock orange.
text.h_s223: It has white flowers that smell sweet.
text.q_s224: Who wrote most of the Declaration of Independence? Is it Thomas Jefferson? Abraham Lincoln? Or George Washington?
text.f_s224: Jefferson's home is called Monticello, and it's on the nickel.
text.q_s225: What is the capital of Canada? Is it Vancouver? Ottawa? Or Toronto?
text.f_s225: Canada has ten provinces and three territories.
text.q_s226: What is the name of the closest galaxy that's like ours? Is it Orion? Pegasus? Or Andromeda?
text.f_s226: You can see Andromeda without a telescope on a very dark night.
text.q_s227: What is the boiling point of water in Celsius? Is it 100 degrees? 212 degrees? Or 50 degrees?
text.f_s227: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius.
text.q_s228: What do you call a scientist who studies animals? Is it A zoologist? A botanist? Or A geologist?
text.h_s228: Zoo is part of the word.
text.q_a001: Boise's statehouse is the only U.S. capitol heated by what? Is it Geothermal water? Natural gas? Solar panels? Or Wood pellets?
text.f_a001: Boise has used geothermal water to heat buildings since the 1890s.
text.q_a002: Apollo astronauts trained at which Idaho national monument? Is it Minidoka? City of Rocks? Hagerman Fossil Beds? Or Craters of the Moon?
text.a_a002: The answer is Craters of the Moon.
text.f_a002: In 1969, Apollo 14 astronauts trained there to learn volcanic geology.
text.q_a003: What is Idaho's official state horse? Is it Appaloosa? Morgan? Mustang? Or Clydesdale?
text.f_a003: The Nez Perce people bred Appaloosas, famous for their spotted coats.
text.q_a004: Which Idaho town was the first in the world lit by nuclear power? Is it Idaho Falls? Blackfoot? Arco? Or Pocatello?
text.f_a004: In 1955, Arco was briefly powered by the BORAX-III reactor.
text.q_a005: Which inventor of electronic television grew up in Rigby, Idaho? Is it John Logie Baird? Thomas Edison? Lee de Forest? Or Philo Farnsworth?
text.f_a005: Farnsworth sketched his idea as a teenager while living near Rigby.
text.q_a006: Which Idaho canyon is the deepest river gorge in North America? Is it Snake River Canyon? Box Canyon? Hells Canyon? Or Bruneau Canyon?
text.f_a006: Hells Canyon is nearly 8,000 feet deep, deeper than the Grand Canyon.
text.q_a007: What is the name of Boise's pro hockey team? Is it Boise Hawks? Idaho Stampede? Idaho Steelheads? Or Treasure Valley Bears?
text.f_a007: The Steelheads play in the ECHL at Idaho Central Arena.
text.q_a008: Which ski resort near Ketchum opened in 1936 with the world's first chairlifts? Is it Sun Valley? Bogus Basin? Brundage? Or Schweitzer?
text.f_a008: The chairlift was adapted from a system for loading bananas onto ships.
text.q_a009: Which Idaho lake is famous for its turquoise color and raspberry shakes? Is it Lake Coeur d'Alene? Bear Lake? Redfish Lake? Or Payette Lake?
text.f_a009: Bear Lake gets its color from limestone particles suspended in the water.
text.q_a010: Coeur d'Alene is French for roughly what? Is it Heart of an awl? Golden heart? Heart of the lake? Or Mountain heart?
text.a_a010: The answer is Heart of an awl.
text.f_a010: French fur traders reportedly used it to describe the sharp trading of the local tribe.
text.q_a011: Which Boise State football game is famous for the Statue of Liberty play? Is it The 2015 Orange Bowl? The 2007 Fiesta Bowl? The 2010 Rose Bowl? Or The 2004 Sugar Bowl?
text.a_a011: The answer is The 2007 Fiesta Bowl.
text.f_a011: Boise State beat Oklahoma 43 to 42 in overtime.
text.q_a012: What is Idaho's state gem? Is it Opal? Sapphire? Star garnet? Or Turquoise?
text.f_a012: Star garnets are found in only Idaho and India in meaningful amounts.
text.q_a013: Sockeye salmon swim about 900 miles to which Idaho lake? Is it Payette Lake? Lake Pend Oreille? Bear Lake? Or Redfish Lake?
text.f_a013: The lake was named for the red sockeye that once filled it.
text.q_a014: What is Idaho's largest lake? Is it Lake Coeur d'Alene? Priest Lake? Lake Pend Oreille? Or Bear Lake?
text.a_a014: The answer is Lake Pend Oreille.
text.f_a014: Lake Pend Oreille is over 1,100 feet deep, and the Navy tests submarine designs there.
text.q_a015: Which famous author lived in Ketchum near the end of his life? Is it F. Scott Fitzgerald? John Steinbeck? Mark Twain? Or Ernest Hemingway?
text.f_a015: Hemingway finished parts of For Whom the Bell Tolls in Sun Valley.
text.q_a016: In what year did Idaho become the 43rd state? Is it 1864? 1912? 1876? Or 1890?
text.f_a016: Idaho was admitted on July 3rd, 1890, a week before Wyoming.
text.q_a017: What is the name of the Boise State mascot? Is it Blaze? Bucky Bronco? Buster Bronco? Or Butch?
text.f_a017: Boise State's blue turf was installed in 1986.
text.q_a018: Which Idaho city is home to the INL, a major national laboratory? Is it Twin Falls? Lewiston? Idaho Falls? Or Moscow?
text.f_a018: More nuclear reactors have been built at INL's site than anywhere else in the world.
text.q_a019: What is Idaho's state motto? Is it Esto perpetua? Dirigo? Excelsior? Or E pluribus unum?
text.f_a019: Esto perpetua means let it be perpetual.
text.q_a020: Which daredevil tried to jump the Snake River Canyon in 1974? Is it Robbie Knievel? Travis Pastrana? Harry Houdini? Or Evel Knievel?
text.f_a020: A parachute deployed early, and he drifted safely to the canyon floor.
text.q_a021: What is the chemical symbol for gold? Is it Go? Ag? Gd? Or Au?
text.f_a021: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.
text.q_a022: What is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere? Is it Nitrogen? Argon? Carbon dioxide? Or Oxygen?
text.f_a022: Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of the air.
text.q_a023: What is the hardest natural substance? Is it Topaz? Titanium? Quartz? Or Diamond?
text.f_a023: Diamond is a 10 on the Mohs hardness scale.
text.q_a024: What is the powerhouse of the cell? Is it Mitochondria? Golgi apparatus? Ribosome? Or Nucleus?
text.f_a024: Mitochondria have their own DNA, inherited from your mother.
text.q_a025: What is the chemical symbol for sodium? Is it S? Na? Sd? Or So?
text.f_a025: Na comes from natrium, its Latin name.
text.q_a026: Which element has the atomic number 1? Is it Carbon? Helium? Hydrogen? Or Oxygen?
text.f_a026: Hydrogen makes up about three quarters of the normal matter in the universe.
text.q_a027: What does DNA stand for? Is it Dinitrogen acid? Dynamic nuclear acid? Dual nucleotide acid? Or Deoxyribonucleic acid?
text.f_a027: Stretched out, the DNA in one human cell would be about six feet long.
text.q_a028: What is the speed of light, roughly? Is it 186,000 miles per second? 18,600 miles per second? 1.8 million miles per second? Or 186,000 miles per hour?
text.a_a028: The answer is 186,000 miles per second.
text.f_a028: Light could circle the Earth about seven and a half times in one second.
text.q_a029: What type of rock is formed from cooled lava? Is it Limestone? Igneous? Sedimentary? Or Metamorphic?
text.f_a029: Basalt, common around Idaho, is an igneous rock.
text.q_a030: Who developed the theory of general relativity? Is it Stephen Hawking? Albert Einstein? Niels Bohr? Or Isaac Newton?
text.q_a031: What is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature? Is it Tin? Gallium? Mercury? Or Lead?
text.f_a031: Gallium melts in your hand, but at room temperature it's solid.
text.q_a032: What is the pH of pure water? Is it 5? 14? 0? Or 7?
text.f_a032: Below 7 is acidic, and above 7 is basic.
text.q_a033: Which scientist is known for the laws of motion? Is it Albert Einstein? Isaac Newton? Galileo Galilei? Or Johannes Kepler?
text.f_a033: Newton also invented an early form of calculus.
text.q_a034: What is the largest organ inside the human body? Is it Liver? Lungs? Brain? Or Heart?
text.f_a034: The liver can regrow to full size after part of it is removed.
text.q_a035: What blood type is known as the universal donor? Is it O negative? B positive? A negative? Or AB positive?
text.f_a035: AB positive is known as the universal recipient.
text.q_a036: What is the main gas in natural gas? Is it Ethane? Methane? Propane? Or Butane?
text.f_a036: Natural gas has no smell. Utilities add an odor for safety.
text.q_a037: What is absolute zero in Celsius, roughly? Is it Minus 100 degrees? Minus 273 degrees? Minus 459 degrees? Or Minus 32 degrees?
text.f_a037: Minus 459 is absolute zero in Fahrenheit.
text.q_a038: Which planet has a day longer than its year? Is it Mars? Venus? Mercury? Or Neptune?
text.f_a038: Venus also spins backward compared with most planets.
text.q_a039: What is the study of fungi called? Is it Entomology? Mycology? Ornithology? Or Botany?
text.f_a039: The largest living organism may be a honey fungus in Oregon.
text.q_a040: Who is credited with discovering penicillin? Is it Jonas Salk? Louis Pasteur? Alexander Fleming? Or Marie Curie?
text.f_a040: Fleming noticed mold killing bacteria in a petri dish in 1928.
text.q_a041: Which scientist was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes? Is it Marie Curie? Albert Einstein? Niels Bohr? Or Linus Pauling?
text.f_a041: She won in physics and in chemistry.
text.q_a042: What does a Geiger counter measure? Is it Radiation? Wind speed? Humidity? Or Earthquakes?
text.f_a042: It clicks for each particle it detects.
text.q_a043: What is the largest volcano in the solar system? Is it Olympus Mons? Mauna Kea? Valles Marineris? Or Mount Everest?
text.f_a043: Olympus Mons is about two and a half times taller than Everest.
text.q_a044: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth? Is it 8 minutes? 80 minutes? 8 hours? Or 8 seconds?
text.f_a044: On average, it takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.
text.q_a045: What was the name of the first artificial satellite? Is it Vostok 1? Telstar? Sputnik 1? Or Explorer 1?
text.f_a045: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik in 1957.
text.q_a046: Which spacecraft is the farthest human-made object from Earth? Is it Pioneer 10? New Horizons? Voyager 2? Or Voyager 1?
text.f_a046: Voyager 1 carries a golden record with sounds and music from Earth.
text.q_a047: Who was the second person to walk on the Moon? Is it Buzz Aldrin? John Glenn? Michael Collins? Or Alan Shepard?
text.f_a047: Michael Collins orbited in the command module during Apollo 11.
text.q_a048: What is the hottest planet in our solar system? Is it Mars? Venus? Jupiter? Or Mercury?
text.f_a048: Venus's surface is hot enough to melt lead.
text.q_a049: Which dwarf planet was reclassified in 2006? Is it Ceres? Eris? Haumea? Or Pluto?
text.f_a049: Pluto has a heart-shaped glacier, nicknamed Tombaugh Regio.
text.q_a050: Which telescope launched in 2021 and sees in infrared? Is it Hubble? Kepler? Spitzer? Or James Webb Space Telescope?
text.a_a050: The answer is James Webb Space Telescope.
text.f_a050: Webb orbits about a million miles from Earth.
text.q_a051: What is the name of the boundary around a black hole? Is it Singularity? Photon belt? Corona? Or Event horizon?
text.f_a051: Not even light can escape from inside the event horizon.
text.q_a052: Which moon of Saturn has a thick atmosphere? Is it Titan? Ganymede? Io? Or Europa?
text.f_a052: Titan has lakes of liquid methane.
text.q_a053: What is the largest moon in the solar system? Is it Our Moon? Ganymede? Titan? Or Callisto?
text.f_a053: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is bigger than the planet Mercury.
text.q_a054: Who was the first American to orbit the Earth? Is it Neil Armstrong? Alan Shepard? John Glenn? Or Gus Grissom?
text.f_a054: Glenn flew again on the space shuttle at age 77.
text.q_a055: What is the closest star system to the Sun? Is it Sirius? Betelgeuse? Vega? Or Alpha Centauri?
text.f_a055: Proxima Centauri is about 4.2 light-years away.
text.q_a056: What is the brightest star in the night sky? Is it Sirius? Betelgeuse? Vega? Or Polaris?
text.f_a056: Sirius is nicknamed the Dog Star.
text.q_a057: What is the capital of Australia? Is it Perth? Melbourne? Sydney? Or Canberra?
text.f_a057: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
text.q_a058: What is the smallest country in the world? Is it San Marino? Monaco? Liechtenstein? Or Vatican City?
text.q_a059: Which country has the most natural lakes? Is it United States? Canada? Russia? Or Finland?
text.f_a059: Canada has more lakes than the rest of the world combined.
text.q_a060: What is the longest mountain range in the world above water? Is it The Alps? The Andes? The Rockies? Or The Himalayas?
text.f_a060: The Andes run about 4,300 miles along South America.
text.q_a061: Which African country has the most pyramids? Is it Sudan? Ethiopia? Egypt? Or Libya?
text.f_a061: Sudan has about 200 ancient pyramids, more than Egypt.
text.q_a062: What is the capital of Canada? Is it Vancouver? Toronto? Ottawa? Or Montreal?
text.f_a062: Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857.
text.q_a063: Which U.S. state has the most coastline? Is it Alaska? California? Hawaii? Or Florida?
text.f_a063: Alaska has more coastline than all other states combined.
text.q_a064: What is the driest place on Earth that isn't a pole? Is it Sahara? Gobi? Atacama Desert? Or Death Valley?
text.f_a064: Some weather stations in the Atacama have never recorded rain.
text.q_a065: Through how many countries does the Danube flow? Is it 13? 10? 7? Or 4?
text.f_a065: The Danube passes through four capital cities, more than any river.
text.q_a066: Which country is home to Machu Picchu? Is it Bolivia? Peru? Chile? Or Ecuador?
text.f_a066: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 1400s.
text.q_a067: What is the deepest point in the ocean? Is it Puerto Rico Trench? Challenger Deep? Java Trench? Or Tonga Trench?
text.f_a067: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is nearly 36,000 feet deep.
text.q_a068: Which state meets Utah, Colorado, and New Mexico at Four Corners? Is it Nevada? Arizona? Wyoming? Or Texas?
text.f_a068: Four Corners is the only spot where four states meet.
text.q_a069: What is the capital of New Zealand? Is it Auckland? Wellington? Queenstown? Or Christchurch?
text.f_a069: Wellington is the southernmost national capital in the world.
text.q_a070: Which is the largest country in South America? Is it Colombia? Brazil? Peru? Or Argentina?
text.f_a070: Brazil borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.
text.q_a071: Which sea is so salty that people float easily in it? Is it The Dead Sea? The Black Sea? The Red Sea? Or The Caspian Sea?
text.a_a071: The answer is The Dead Sea.
text.f_a071: The Dead Sea's shore is the lowest land on Earth.
text.q_a072: What is the most populous U.S. state? Is it California? Florida? New York? Or Texas?
text.f_a072: About one in eight Americans lives in California.
text.q_a073: Which river flows through Baghdad? Is it Euphrates? Nile? Jordan? Or Tigris?
text.f_a073: The Tigris and Euphrates frame ancient Mesopotamia.
text.q_a074: What is the largest hot desert in the world? Is it Kalahari? Sahara? Gobi? Or Arabian?
text.f_a074: Antarctica is technically the largest desert overall.
text.q_a075: Which European city is built on 118 small islands? Is it Stockholm? Copenhagen? Venice? Or Amsterdam?
text.q_a076: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall? Is it 1985? 1989? 1991? Or 1979?
text.f_a076: The wall had divided Berlin for 28 years.
text.q_a077: Who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic? Is it Bessie Coleman? Harriet Quimby? Amelia Earhart? Or Sally Ride?
text.q_a078: Which U.S. President served the shortest term? Is it William Henry Harrison? James Garfield? Zachary Taylor? Or John Tyler?
text.a_a078: The answer is William Henry Harrison.
text.q_a079: What year did the first Moon landing happen? Is it 1965? 1972? 1969? Or 1959?
text.f_a079: About 600 million people watched it on TV.
text.q_a080: Which ancient wonder was in Alexandria? Is it The Hanging Gardens? The Temple of Artemis? The Lighthouse? Or The Colossus?
text.f_a080: The Lighthouse of Alexandria stood for over a thousand years.
text.q_a081: Who was the only U.S. President to serve more than two terms? Is it Theodore Roosevelt? Woodrow Wilson? Ulysses S. Grant? Or Franklin D. Roosevelt?
text.a_a081: The answer is Franklin D. Roosevelt.
text.f_a081: The 22nd Amendment later limited presidents to two terms.
text.q_a082: What was the first capital of the United States under the Constitution? Is it Philadelphia? New York City? Washington, D.C.? Or Boston?
text.a_a082: The answer is New York City.
text.f_a082: George Washington was inaugurated on Wall Street in 1789.
text.q_a083: Who painted the Mona Lisa? Is it Rembrandt? Raphael? Michelangelo? Or Leonardo da Vinci?
text.a_a083: The answer is Leonardo da Vinci.
text.f_a083: The Mona Lisa has no visible eyebrows.
text.q_a084: What was the name of the ship that carried Charles Darwin? Is it HMS Beagle? HMS Victory? HMS Bounty? Or HMS Endeavour?
text.f_a084: Darwin's voyage lasted almost five years.
text.q_a085: What did the 19th Amendment do? Is it Ended slavery? Created income tax? Gave women the right to vote? Or Lowered the voting age?
text.a_a085: The answer is Gave women the right to vote.
text.q_a086: Which empire built Machu Picchu? Is it Inca? Aztec? Maya? Or Olmec?
text.f_a086: The Inca built it without mortar, fitting stones tightly together.
text.q_a087: Who invented the telephone, according to the first U.S. patent? Is it Thomas Edison? Samuel Morse? Nikola Tesla? Or Alexander Graham Bell?
text.a_a087: The answer is Alexander Graham Bell.
text.f_a087: Bell's first words on it were Mr. Watson, come here.
text.q_a088: Which country gifted the Statue of Liberty to the U.S.? Is it France? Italy? England? Or Spain?
text.f_a088: Gustave Eiffel designed its internal frame.
text.q_a089: In what year was the Louisiana Purchase? Is it 1848? 1776? 1812? Or 1803?
text.f_a089: It roughly doubled the size of the United States.
text.q_a090: Who was the first U.S. President to live in the White House? Is it George Washington? Thomas Jefferson? John Adams? Or James Madison?
text.f_a090: Adams moved in in 1800, while it was still unfinished.
text.q_a091: What was the name of the first successful English colony in America? Is it Jamestown? Boston? Roanoke? Or Plymouth?
text.f_a091: Jamestown was founded in Virginia in 1607.
text.q_a092: What was Benjamin Franklin's famous almanac called? Is it Franklin's Guide? The Colonial Times? Poor Richard's Almanack? Or The Farmer's Almanac?
text.a_a092: The answer is Poor Richard's Almanack.
text.f_a092: It's the source of early to bed, early to rise.
text.q_a093: Which famous trail crossed southern Idaho on the way to the Pacific Northwest? Is it The Santa Fe Trail? The Oregon Trail? The Mormon Trail? Or The Chisholm Trail?
text.a_a093: The answer is The Oregon Trail.
text.f_a093: Wagon ruts from the Oregon Trail are still visible near Boise.
text.q_a094: What is the oldest university in the United States? Is it Yale? William and Mary? Harvard? Or Princeton?
text.q_a095: In The Little Mermaid, what does Ariel call a fork? Is it A thingamabob? A snarfblatt? A whozit? Or A dinglehopper?
text.f_a095: Scuttle calls a pipe a snarfblatt.
text.q_a096: What was Pixar's first full-length feature film? Is it Monsters, Inc.? A Bug's Life? Finding Nemo? Or Toy Story?
text.f_a096: Toy Story, in 1995, was the first fully computer-animated feature.
text.q_a097: What is the name of the kingdom in Frozen? Is it Arendelle? Corona? DunBroch? Or Agrabah?
text.q_a098: In The Wizard of Oz, what color are Dorothy's slippers in the movie? Is it Gold? Emerald green? Ruby red? Or Silver?
text.f_a098: In the original book, they were silver.
text.q_a099: Which Disney movie features the song Hakuna Matata? Is it Tarzan? The Lion King? The Jungle Book? Or Aladdin?
text.a_a099: The answer is The Lion King.
text.f_a099: Hakuna matata is Swahili for no worries.
text.q_a100: In Back to the Future, what speed must the DeLorean reach to time travel? Is it 121 miles per hour? 88 miles per hour? 100 miles per hour? Or 55 miles per hour?
text.a_a100: The answer is 88 miles per hour.
text.q_a101: Who voiced Woody in Toy Story? Is it Tom Hanks? Billy Crystal? Tim Allen? Or Robin Williams?
text.q_a102: In Up, what is the name of the talking dog? Is it Carl? Russell? Kevin? Or Dug?
text.q_a103: Which film won the first Academy Award for Best Animated Feature? Is it Shrek? Finding Nemo? Monsters, Inc.? Or Spirited Away?
text.q_a104: In The Princess Bride, what is Westley's catchphrase to Buttercup? Is it Have fun storming the castle? Inconceivable? As you wish? Or Hello, my name is?
text.a_a104: The answer is As you wish.
text.q_a105: In Ratatouille, what is the rat's name? Is it Gusteau? Remy? Emile? Or Linguini?
text.f_a105: Remy lives by the motto anyone can cook.
text.q_a106: Who composed the music for Star Wars and Jurassic Park? Is it Hans Zimmer? John Williams? Danny Elfman? Or Howard Shore?
text.f_a106: John Williams has more than 50 Oscar nominations.
text.q_a107: What color is the pill Neo takes in The Matrix? Is it White? Red? Blue? Or Green?
text.f_a107: The blue pill would have returned him to his old life.
text.q_a108: In The Sound of Music, how many von Trapp children are there? Is it 5? 8? 6? Or 7?
text.f_a108: The real von Trapp family eventually settled in Vermont.
text.q_a109: Which Disney princess is from the kingdom of Corona? Is it Belle? Merida? Aurora? Or Rapunzel?
text.q_a110: In Monsters, Inc., what powers the city of Monstropolis at first? Is it Candy? Laughs? Screams? Or Lightning?
text.f_a110: By the end, they discover laughter is even more powerful.
text.q_a111: What is the name of the hobbit played by Elijah Wood? Is it Pippin Took? Samwise Gamgee? Bilbo Baggins? Or Frodo Baggins?
text.f_a111: The films were shot in New Zealand.
text.q_a112: What fictional African country is the home of Black Panther? Is it Zamunda? Wakanda? Genovia? Or Latveria?
text.q_a113: Which band sang Here Comes the Sun? Is it The Beach Boys? The Beatles? The Monkees? Or The Rolling Stones?
text.f_a113: George Harrison wrote it in Eric Clapton's garden.
text.q_a114: Who is known as the King of Pop? Is it Michael Jackson? Prince? Elvis Presley? Or Justin Timberlake?
text.f_a114: Thriller is one of the best-selling albums of all time.
text.q_a115: Which artist's fan base is called Swifties? Is it Katy Perry? Taylor Swift? Ariana Grande? Or Selena Gomez?
text.f_a115: The Eras Tour became the highest-grossing concert tour ever.
text.q_a116: How many keys does a standard piano have? Is it 61? 100? 76? Or 88?
text.f_a116: There are 52 white keys and 36 black keys.
text.q_a117: Who wrote the opera The Magic Flute? Is it Mozart? Wagner? Beethoven? Or Verdi?
text.f_a117: Mozart wrote it in the last year of his life.
text.q_a118: Which instrument did Louis Armstrong famously play? Is it Clarinet? Saxophone? Trumpet? Or Trombone?
text.q_a119: What is the name of Elvis Presley's Memphis home? Is it Graceland? Neverland? Mar-a-Lago? Or Monticello?
text.f_a119: Graceland is one of the most visited homes in America.
text.q_a120: Which band recorded Bohemian Rhapsody? Is it Led Zeppelin? The Who? Queen? Or Pink Floyd?
text.f_a120: The song has no repeating chorus.
text.q_a121: Which country singer is known for the song Jolene? Is it Dolly Parton? Shania Twain? Reba McEntire? Or Loretta Lynn?
text.f_a121: Dolly also wrote I Will Always Love You.
text.q_a122: What is the term for a group of three musical notes played together? Is it A riff? An octave? A scale? Or A chord?
text.f_a122: A major chord sounds bright, and a minor chord sounds sadder.
text.q_a123: Which composer wrote The Nutcracker ballet? Is it Bach? Stravinsky? Mozart? Or Tchaikovsky?
text.f_a123: The Nutcracker premiered in 1892 in Saint Petersburg.
text.q_a124: What is the best-selling single of all time? Is it White Christmas? Shape of You? Candle in the Wind? Or Hey Jude?
text.f_a124: Bing Crosby's White Christmas has sold an estimated 50 million copies.
text.q_a125: How many players are on a baseball team on the field? Is it 10? 9? 11? Or 8?
text.f_a125: A regulation game is nine innings.
text.q_a126: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cups? Is it Germany? Argentina? Brazil? Or Italy?
text.f_a126: Brazil has won five World Cups.
text.q_a127: In golf, what is one stroke under par called? Is it Albatross? Birdie? Eagle? Or Bogey?
text.f_a127: Two under par is an eagle.
text.q_a128: Which athlete has won the most Olympic medals? Is it Simone Biles? Carl Lewis? Michael Phelps? Or Usain Bolt?
text.f_a128: Phelps won 28 Olympic medals, 23 of them gold.
text.q_a129: How long is a marathon? Is it 30 miles? 24.5 miles? 26.2 miles? Or 20 miles?
text.f_a129: The distance was standardized after the 1908 London Olympics.
text.q_a130: What sport is played at Wimbledon? Is it Golf? Tennis? Cricket? Or Polo?
text.f_a130: Players must wear almost all white.
text.q_a131: How many points is a field goal in football? Is it 2? 6? 3? Or 1?
text.f_a131: A safety is worth two points.
text.q_a132: In which city is the Basketball Hall of Fame? Is it Springfield, Massachusetts? Chicago? Indianapolis? Or New York?
text.f_a132: Basketball was invented in Springfield in 1891.
text.q_a133: What is the maximum score in a single game of bowling? Is it 250? 350? 200? Or 300?
text.f_a133: A 300 game is twelve strikes in a row.
text.q_a134: What is the diameter of a basketball hoop? Is it 16 inches? 18 inches? 24 inches? Or 12 inches?
text.f_a134: A basketball can almost fit through it side by side twice.
text.q_a135: In tennis, what is a score of 40 to 40 called? Is it Break? Love? Advantage? Or Deuce?
text.f_a135: From deuce, a player must win two points in a row.
text.q_a136: Which sport uses the terms stone, sweep, and house? Is it Bocce? Curling? Shuffleboard? Or Lawn bowling?
text.f_a136: Curling stones are made from granite, much of it from one Scottish island.
text.q_a137: How many minutes long is an NBA game, not counting overtime? Is it 40? 48? 45? Or 60?
text.q_a138: Which country invented the sport of judo? Is it Brazil? Korea? China? Or Japan?
text.q_a139: Which spice is the most expensive by weight? Is it Vanilla? Cardamom? Cinnamon? Or Saffron?
text.f_a139: Saffron threads are hand-picked from crocus flowers.
text.q_a140: What fruit is used to make the drink cider? Is it Grapes? Peaches? Apples? Or Pears?
text.q_a141: Which country is the original home of the potato? Is it Peru? Idaho? Russia? Or Ireland?
text.f_a141: Potatoes were first grown in the Andes thousands of years ago.
text.q_a142: What is the main ingredient in traditional Japanese miso? Is it Rice? Fish? Soybeans? Or Seaweed?
text.q_a143: Which nut is used to make marzipan? Is it Pistachio? Hazelnut? Almond? Or Cashew?
text.f_a143: Marzipan is almond flour and sugar.
text.q_a144: What is the most consumed beverage in the world after water? Is it Milk? Coffee? Tea? Or Soda?
text.f_a144: Turkey drinks the most tea per person.
text.q_a145: What type of pastry is used for profiteroles and éclairs? Is it Puff pastry? Choux pastry? Phyllo dough? Or Shortcrust?
text.f_a145: Choux pastry puffs up from steam.
text.q_a146: Which fruit has its seeds on the outside? Is it Kiwi? Blueberry? Strawberry? Or Raspberry?
text.q_a147: What gives chili peppers their heat? Is it Capsaicin? Tannin? Menthol? Or Lycopene?
text.f_a147: Heat is measured on the Scoville scale.
text.q_a148: Which cheese is traditionally used on a Caesar salad? Is it Parmesan? Cheddar? Feta? Or Blue cheese?
text.f_a148: Caesar salad was invented in Tijuana, Mexico.
text.q_a149: What is a restaurant's wine expert called? Is it Barista? Maître d'? Chef de cuisine? Or Sommelier?
text.f_a149: The Master Sommelier exam is one of the hardest tests in the world.
text.q_a150: What is the national dish of Spain, made with rice? Is it Risotto? Paella? Jambalaya? Or Biryani?
text.q_a151: What is the most widely produced fruit in the world? Is it Oranges? Bananas? Apples? Or Watermelons?
text.f_a151: Most bananas sold are the Cavendish variety.
text.q_a152: Fortune cookies were popularized in which country? Is it The United States? China? Korea? Or Japan?
text.a_a152: The answer is The United States.
text.f_a152: They likely trace back to Japanese bakeries in California.
text.q_a153: How many hearts does an octopus have? Is it 8? 1? 2? Or 3?
text.f_a153: Octopus blood is blue because it uses copper.
text.q_a154: What is a group of flamingos called? Is it A congregation? A blush? A flamboyance? Or A parade?
text.f_a154: Flamingos are pink because of the shrimp and algae they eat.
text.q_a155: What is the only mammal capable of true flight? Is it Colugo? Sugar glider? Bat? Or Flying squirrel?
text.f_a155: Bats make up about a fifth of all mammal species.
text.q_a156: Which animal has the longest pregnancy? Is it Giraffe? Elephant? Blue whale? Or Rhinoceros?
text.q_a157: What is a baby kangaroo called? Is it Joey? Cub? Kid? Or Pup?
text.f_a157: A newborn joey is about the size of a jelly bean.
text.q_a158: Which bird can fly backward? Is it Kingfisher? Hummingbird? Swift? Or Sparrow?
text.f_a158: Hummingbird hearts can beat over 1,000 times a minute.
text.q_a159: What is the largest living species of lizard? Is it Gila monster? Monitor lizard? Komodo dragon? Or Green iguana?
text.f_a159: Komodo dragons live on a few Indonesian islands.
text.q_a160: How many stomach compartments does a cow have? Is it 2? 6? 1? Or 4?
text.f_a160: The first compartment is called the rumen.
text.q_a161: What animal has fingerprints almost identical to humans? Is it Gorilla? Raccoon? Koala? Or Chimpanzee?
text.f_a161: Koala prints are hard to tell apart from people's even under a microscope.
text.q_a162: What is the fastest bird in a dive? Is it Peregrine falcon? Golden eagle? Swift? Or Albatross?
text.f_a162: Peregrines can dive at over 200 miles per hour.
text.q_a163: What do you call a group of owls? Is it A congress? A senate? A parliament? Or A council?
text.f_a163: Owls can't move their eyes, so they turn their heads instead.
text.q_a164: Which animal sleeps the most per day, on average? Is it Koala? Lion? Sloth? Or Cat?
text.f_a164: Koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day.
text.q_a165: What is the national bird of the United States? Is it Wild turkey? American robin? Golden eagle? Or Bald eagle?
text.f_a165: Ben Franklin reportedly preferred the turkey.
text.q_a166: A tardigrade is also known as what? Is it Water bear? Sea mouse? Moss pig? Or Rock flea?
text.f_a166: Tardigrades can survive in the vacuum of space.
text.q_a167: How many bones are in the adult human body? Is it 216? 206? 256? Or 186?
text.f_a167: More than half of them are in your hands and feet.
text.q_a168: What is the smallest bone in the human body? Is it Incus? Stapes? Hyoid? Or Malleus?
text.f_a168: The stapes is in the middle ear.
text.q_a169: About how many times does an adult heart beat in a day? Is it 50,000? 1,000,000? 100,000? Or 10,000?
text.f_a169: At about 70 beats a minute, that's roughly 100,000.
text.q_a170: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination? Is it Cerebrum? Cerebellum? Brain stem? Or Hypothalamus?
text.q_a171: What is the hardest substance in the human body? Is it Bone? Cartilage? Fingernail? Or Tooth enamel?
text.f_a171: Enamel can't repair itself once it's damaged.
text.q_a172: Which organ produces insulin? Is it Liver? Kidney? Spleen? Or Pancreas?
text.f_a172: Insulin was first used to treat diabetes in 1922.
text.q_a173: How many chambers does the human heart have? Is it 3? 6? 4? Or 2?
text.f_a173: The two lower chambers are called ventricles.
text.q_a174: What is the most common blood type in the U.S.? Is it A positive? O positive? AB negative? Or B positive?
text.f_a174: About 38 percent of people have O positive blood.
text.q_a175: What is a word that reads the same backward and forward? Is it Homonym? Palindrome? Anagram? Or Acronym?
text.q_a176: What does the abbreviation e.g. stand for? Is it Et gratia? Exactly given? Example given? Or Exempli gratia?
text.f_a176: It means for example, while i.e. means that is.
text.q_a177: Which language has the most native speakers? Is it Spanish? Hindi? English? Or Mandarin Chinese?
text.f_a177: Spanish is second for native speakers.
text.q_a178: Saying the opposite of what you mean, for effect, is called what? Is it Alliteration? Hyperbole? Metaphor? Or Irony?
text.f_a178: Situational irony is when the opposite of what you expect happens.
text.q_a179: What is the term for a word formed from the first letters of other words, like NASA? Is it Antonym? Acronym? Synonym? Or Homophone?
text.f_a179: NASA stands for National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
text.q_a180: What is the most common letter in English? Is it E? A? S? Or T?
text.f_a180: The least common letter is usually Q or Z.
text.q_a181: What sentence uses every letter of the alphabet? Is it Pack my box with jam? The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog? Every good boy does fine? Or A journey of a thousand miles?
text.a_a181: The answer is The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
text.f_a181: Sentences like this are called pangrams.
text.q_a182: Which Shakespeare play features the line To be or not to be? Is it King Lear? Othello? Hamlet? Or Macbeth?
text.f_a182: Shakespeare added hundreds of words to English.
text.q_a183: Who wrote Charlotte's Web? Is it Beverly Cleary? E. B. White? Roald Dahl? Or Dr. Seuss?
text.a_a183: The answer is E. B. White.
text.f_a183: E. B. White also wrote Stuart Little.
text.q_a184: Who wrote the Harry Potter books? Is it C. S. Lewis? Suzanne Collins? Rick Riordan? Or J. K. Rowling?
text.a_a184: The answer is J. K. Rowling.
text.f_a184: The first book was published in 1997.
text.q_a185: In The Chronicles of Narnia, what is the lion's name? Is it Leo? Caspian? Aslan? Or Mufasa?
text.f_a185: C. S. Lewis was friends with J. R. R. Tolkien.
text.q_a186: What Dr. Seuss book was written using only 50 different words? Is it The Cat in the Hat? Hop on Pop? Fox in Socks? Or Green Eggs and Ham?
text.a_a186: The answer is Green Eggs and Ham.
text.f_a186: It started as a bet with his publisher.
text.q_a187: In The Twelve Days of Christmas, how many lords are a-leaping? Is it 12? 10? 11? Or 9?
text.f_a187: Add up every gift across all twelve days, and you get 364.
text.q_a188: Which country started the tradition of the Christmas tree? Is it England? Sweden? Norway? Or Germany?
text.f_a188: Prince Albert helped popularize the tree in England.
text.q_a189: What is the name of the Grinch's dog? Is it Fido? Max? Cindy Lou? Or Buddy?
text.f_a189: Dr. Seuss published How the Grinch Stole Christmas in 1957.
text.q_a190: Which holiday is celebrated on March 17th? Is it Pi Day? Earth Day? St. Patrick's Day? Or Groundhog Day?
text.a_a190: The answer is St. Patrick's Day.
text.f_a190: Chicago dyes its river green for it every year.
text.q_a191: Pi Day is celebrated on what date? Is it February 14th? March 14th? March 3rd? Or April 1st?
text.q_a192: What is the Hindu festival of lights called? Is it Navratri? Pongal? Holi? Or Diwali?
text.q_a193: In what year did Thanksgiving become a national holiday? Is it 1863? 1941? 1776? Or 1621?
text.f_a193: Sarah Josepha Hale, who wrote Mary Had a Little Lamb, campaigned for it.
text.q_a194: Which reindeer is NOT one of Santa's original eight? Is it Comet? Blitzen? Rudolph? Or Cupid?
text.f_a194: Rudolph came from a 1939 department store booklet.
text.q_a195: What flower is traditionally given on Mother's Day in the U.S.? Is it Rose? Tulip? Lily? Or Carnation?
text.f_a195: Founder Anna Jarvis chose white carnations for her mother.
text.q_a196: What year did the U.S. celebrate its semiquincentennial? Is it 2076? 2026? 2025? Or 2016?
text.q_a197: Which TV neighborhood was led by Fred Rogers? Is it Zoom? Sesame Street? Reading Rainbow? Or Mister Rogers' Neighborhood?
text.a_a197: The answer is Mister Rogers' Neighborhood.
text.f_a197: Fred Rogers changed into his sneakers at the start of every episode.
text.q_a198: What street do Big Bird and Elmo live on? Is it Maple Street? Elm Street? Sesame Street? Or Rainbow Road?
text.q_a199: In The Office, what is the name of the paper company? Is it Dunder Mifflin? Vance Refrigeration? Sabre? Or Wernham Hogg?
text.f_a199: The office branch is in Scranton, Pennsylvania.
text.q_a200: Which cartoon family lives in Springfield? Is it The Griffins? The Flintstones? The Simpsons? Or The Jetsons?
text.f_a200: The Simpsons is the longest-running American scripted primetime series.
text.q_a201: In Bluey, what is the name of Bluey's dad? Is it Rusty? Stripe? Chilli? Or Bandit?
text.f_a201: Bluey is made in Brisbane, Australia.
text.q_a202: What is the name of the coffee shop in Friends? Is it Moonbeans? The Grind? Java Joe's? Or Central Perk?
text.f_a202: The orange couch was found in the Warner Bros. basement.
text.q_a203: Which game show asks contestants to phrase answers as questions? Is it Family Feud? The Price Is Right? Jeopardy!? Or Wheel of Fortune?
text.f_a203: Ken Jennings won 74 games in a row.
text.q_a204: In Star Trek, what is the name of Captain Kirk's ship? Is it Millennium Falcon? USS Voyager? USS Enterprise? Or Serenity?
text.q_a205: What does www stand for in a web address? Is it World Wide Web? World Web Wire? Web World Wide? Or Wide World Web?
text.a_a205: The answer is World Wide Web.
text.f_a205: Tim Berners-Lee invented the web in 1989.
text.q_a206: What was the first name of Apple's co-founder Wozniak? Is it Larry? Bill? Paul? Or Steve?
text.f_a206: Both Apple founders were named Steve.
text.q_a207: What company makes the PlayStation? Is it Nintendo? Sony? Sega? Or Microsoft?
text.f_a207: The first PlayStation launched in 1994 in Japan.
text.q_a208: Which Nintendo character is a plumber? Is it Kirby? Link? Mario? Or Sonic?
text.q_a209: What year was the first iPhone released? Is it 2004? 2009? 2010? Or 2007?
text.f_a209: The first iPhone had no app store.
text.q_a210: What does GPS stand for? Is it General Pointing Satellite? Global Positioning System? Geographic Path Service? Or Global Path Signal?
text.a_a210: The answer is Global Positioning System.
text.f_a210: GPS uses about 30 satellites run by the U.S. Space Force.
text.q_a211: What does the Q in QR code stand for? Is it Quantum? Query? Quick? Or Quality?
text.f_a211: QR codes were invented in Japan to track car parts.
